doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Calling himself a versatile drummer
summary: Asked if he is a journeyman drummer, Caputo says he is versatile and borrows from every style for his jazz playing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You’re welcome. As I’m looking at your list of people you’ve played with, it goes from Joan Rivers to Cab Calloway, to Darius Brubeck, and I’m thinking of the term “journeyman drummer.” Do you call yourself a journeyman drummer?

I call myself versatile. I call myself versatile. Yes. And I play any style and thus, I like to, it helps with my discipline, playing the shows, and I use that discipline in my jazz playing. So I’m a versatile player, I play all styles, and I enjoy that, it keeps me fresh, and I kind of steal from each one of those styles and institute it in my jazz playing.
